zoe: spotted a docs drift in the Go quickstart. auth header is added after request and the sample uses a blocking ReadAll that can leak goroutines under load. saw in a partner POC.
kai: where is it?
zoe: quickstart/go/README.md 
bad snippet:```go
client := &http.Client{}
resp, err := client.Post(url, body) // auth header missing
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
bodyBytes, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body) // no defer resp.Body.Close()
```
sam: ugh: header set after the request, and no resp.Body.Close -> file descriptor leaks. also no retry handling for 429 or Retry-After.
zoe: propose fix: set header on the request before send, use defer resp.Body.Close(), and mention simple retry with backoff or use go-retryablehttp in prod.
kai: add a tiny code sample showing building the request first and defer close. also add a note about context.WithTimeout to avoid goroutine leaks.
sam: can we add a small test in docs CI that `go vet` or `go test` the sample package so it gets basic linting?
zoe: yes i will open a PR that: updates README snippet, adds a short paragraph on retry/Retry-After, and requests the CI job. tagging @kai for review.
docs-bot: created issue #4210 for Go quickstart fixes (assign: zoe).
zoe: thanks, landing asap to avoid more copy/paste pain during demos.
